title: One Ångström Where Two Neurons Wire Together — Ebbinghaus's 1885 Savings Curve, Hebb's Postulate & Lømo's 1966 Rabbit LTP, GluN1/GluN2B NMDA Coincidence Architecture (PDB 4PE5), Cryo-EM Proof of the Asn616/Asn615 Mg2+ Pore Cork (PDB 9IYP) & S-Ketamine Block (PDB 7EU7), and Lisman, Schulman & Kuriyan's 12-Subunit CaMKII Thr286 Memory Hub (PDB 3SOA, 2VZ6, 2WEL)

teenKit.tldr: Memories aren't ethereal ghosts floating in your head—they are physical, atomic-level alterations built into the architecture of your brain cells. By shrinking down to the scale of a single angstrom, we can actually see how molecules like NMDA and CaMKII lock experiences into place.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding the exact atomic hardware of memory changes how we tackle everything from learning a new language to treating traumatic brain injuries and neurological disorders.
keyTakeaways: Memories take up physical space and require actual structural changes in brain tissue, meaning every memory has a literal weight and molecular address.
The NMDA receptor acts like a molecular coincidence detector, requiring two separate conditions to open and let signals pass through.
Proteins like CaMKII function as massive 12-subunit memory hubs that lock in signals to make sure short-term experiences become permanent memories.

vocab.meaning: An ultra-tiny unit of measurement equal to one ten-billionth of a meter, where a single carbon-to-carbon bond stands about shoulder height to someone shrunk to that scale.
A specialized protein channel in neuron synapses that acts as a coincidence detector to trigger learning and memory formation.
A magnesium ion that physically blocks the NMDA receptor channel like a cork in a bottle until electrical activity knocks it out of the way.
A complex, 12-subunit protein hub that acts as a molecular memory switch by remembering past electrical storms in the brain.

quiz.question: What is the central physical truth about a memory explored in the podcast?
options: It is a purely spiritual phenomenon that leaves no trace on matter.
It is a physical, measurable structural alteration that takes up space in brain tissue.
It only exists while you are actively speaking out loud.
It is stored entirely in the blood cells rather than the brain.
quiz.explanation: Memories are not ghosts; they require physical space, energy, and structural changes in neural tissue.

quiz.question: At the scale of one angstrom, what object would stand roughly shoulder-height to you?
options: A single carbon-to-carbon bond inside a molecule
quiz.explanation: At the one-angstrom scale, a single carbon-to-carbon molecular bond is large enough to stand about shoulder-height to a human observer.

quiz.question: What role does the magnesium ion play in the NMDA receptor channel?
options: It acts as a chemical fuel source for the neuron.
It speeds up the transmission of sound waves.
It acts as a pore cork, blocking the channel until the right electrical conditions are met.
quiz.explanation: The magnesium ion sits in the pore like a cork, blocking ion flow until electrical depolarization kicks it out.
